learning.title: Editing an applied migration file, even a comment, breaks every database lane on that stack
learning.trigger: A migration file that a stack's database has already applied is edited again in the same branch.
learning.mistake: A comment-only edit of an applied migration changes its checksum. The ledger still holds the old one, so every database lane on that stack fails with MIGRATION_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH:<version>, and the failure reads like a code defect in whichever lane runs first.
learning.rule: Finish the migration text before the first apply, and make any later edit its own step. After one, reset only the stack you own with `pnpm --dir apps/server reset` (confirmation variables come from that stack's env file; a Docker-hosted stack also needs `BAKERY_TEST_DATABASE_ALLOW_REMOTE_RESET=1` because the server sees a container address, so first confirm the published port maps to your own project's container, and take the verification flock) before rerunning lanes. A reviewer who meets the mismatch stops and reports the ledger evidence instead of resetting a database it does not own.

verification.requirement: After the reset, a database lane that applies the migration starts and reports no checksum mismatch.
